checks.describe: list_workflow_runs() builds exactly one httpx.Client() and reuses it across every paginated request, instead of opening a new client per page
the backoff delay grows exponentially with the attempt number (base * 2**attempt), the formula section 3 walks through
the backoff delay adds a random jitter term on top of the exponential base -- the fix for the synchronized-retry stampede the jitter simulation demonstrates
MAX_RETRIES is set to 4, the value the retry-exhaustion tests and the flaky-server demo rely on
RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES names only 429 and the 5xx family -- never a permanent 4xx like 401 or 404
401 (a permanent client error) is never in the retryable set -- section 3's idempotency argument depends on this
_request_with_retry() is only ever invoked with the GET method inside httpclient.py -- proof the retry-safety argument (idempotent reads only) holds in the real code, not just in prose

the four mocked retry/no-retry scenarios (429-then-success, 500-exhausts, 401-never-retried, connection-failure-exhausts) pass against the frozen checkpoint -- the same behavior the flaky-server demo exercises live
checks.run: cd labs/checkpoints/v0.7 && uv run pytest -q -k 'retries or does_not_retry' 2>&1

checks.describe: an httpx.Client(http2=True) can be built once the optional h2 package is available -- proof HTTP/2 support is an opt-in flag, not a missing feature
checks.run: cd labs/checkpoints/v0.7 && uv run --with h2 python3 -c "import httpx; client = httpx.Client(http2=True); print('constructed-ok'); client.close()"

checks.describe: reusing one httpx.Client() across N requests to the same host is faster than opening a fresh client per request -- the keep-alive claim section 1 makes, checked as a real timing comparison against a live endpoint
checks.run:
cd labs/checkpoints/v0.7 && uv run python3 -c "import time; import httpx; N=6; URL='https://api.github.com'
start=time.perf_counter()
with httpx.Client() as c:
    for _ in range(N): c.get(URL)
reused=time.perf_counter()-start
start=time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(N):
    with httpx.Client() as c: c.get(URL)
fresh=time.perf_counter()-start
print('faster' if reused < fresh else 'not-faster')"
